title: It Is a Comely Thing
description: It Is a Comely Thing in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns of the Greek Church (Edinburgh and London, 1900).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Short Metre (6.6.8.6), and this page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: It is a come-ly thing To glo-ri-fy and praise Our God, the Ev-er-last-ing Word, And Lord of end-less days.

lines: And all the heavenly hosts adore
O Christ, to Thee we pray,
For Thou didst break the bands of death
To Thee, Thou Three in One,
One power, one kingdom without end,
O Christ, the source of light,
Come, make my heart the bright abode

source: John Brownlie, Hymns of the Greek Church (1900)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns of the Greek Church; set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
